fr: la durée légale du travail (35 heures)
def: The statutory working week in France: 35 hours for a full-time employee, above which hours count as overtime.

formal.ex: The [[statutory working week]] in France is thirty-five hours; any hours worked beyond that threshold attract overtime compensation.
formal.ex_us: The [[statutory workweek]] in France is thirty-five hours; any hours worked beyond that threshold trigger overtime compensation.

everyday.ex: People assume [[the 35-hour week]] is a cap, but it's really just the point where overtime kicks in.
everyday.ex_us: People assume [[the 35-hour workweek]] is a cap, but it's really just the point where overtime kicks in.

note_fr: Les 35 heures sont un seuil de déclenchement des heures supplémentaires, pas un plafond : c'est le contresens le plus répandu chez les interlocuteurs étrangers. Ne dites pas « legal duration of work » (calque) mais « statutory working week ». US : « workweek » en un mot ; le seuil fédéral des heures supplémentaires y est de 40 heures.

explain.written: the statutory working week of thirty-five hours, which is the threshold above which overtime is payable rather than a maximum
explain.spoken: In France the standard week is 35 hours. You can work more than that - it just counts as overtime.

def: Hours worked in addition to an employee's normal or statutory working hours.

formal.ex: Any [[overtime hours]] must be authorised in advance by the Employee's line manager.
formal.ex_us: Any [[overtime hours]] must be authorized in advance by the Employee's supervisor.

everyday.ex: We've had a lot of [[overtime]] in the warehouse this month.

informal.ex: He's been picking up plenty of [[OT]] on the weekend shifts.

note_fr: « Overtime » est indénombrable : on dit « ten hours of overtime », jamais « ten overtimes » ni « supplementary hours » (calque). Aux États-Unis, seuls les salariés « non-exempt » y ont droit ; au Royaume-Uni, la loi n'impose aucune majoration, tout dépend du contrat.

def: To work more hours than your normal working time.

formal.ex: Employees may be required [[to work overtime]] where the needs of the business so demand.

everyday.ex: I can [[do overtime]] on Thursday if you're short-staffed.
everyday.ex_us: I can [[work overtime]] on Thursday if you're short-staffed.

informal.ex: The whole team [[put in extra hours]] to get the payroll out on time.

collocations: to be asked to work overtime
note_fr: On dit « to work overtime » ou, au Royaume-Uni, « to do overtime » ; jamais « to make overtime » (calque de « faire »). En France, le salarié ne peut en principe pas refuser les heures supplémentaires demandées dans les limites légales : précisez-le à un Britannique, pour qui tout dépend du contrat.

def: A plan showing which employees work at which times.

formal.ex: The [[work schedule]] shall be communicated to employees no later than seven days in advance.

everyday.ex: Has next week's [[rota]] gone up yet?
everyday.ex_us: Has next week's [[schedule]] been posted yet?

note_fr: « Planning » n'existe pas dans ce sens en anglais : dites « rota » (UK, pour le travail en équipes) ou « schedule » (US et universel). Prononciation de « schedule » : /ˈʃedjuːl/ au Royaume-Uni, /ˈskedʒuːl/ aux États-Unis.

def: To record the time you start or finish work, usually on a machine or an app.

formal.uk: to record one's arrival and departure times
formal.us: to record one's arrival and departure times
formal.ex: All hourly-paid staff are required [[to record their arrival and departure times]] using the electronic system.

everyday.ex: Don't forget to [[clock in]] when you get to the site.

informal.ex: She [[punched in]] ten minutes late again this morning.

note_fr: « To clock in / on » à l'arrivée, « to clock out / off » au départ. « To punch in / out » est surtout américain. Faux ami : « to point » ne veut jamais dire pointer. La badgeuse : « time clock ».

def: A record of the hours or days an employee has worked, often split by task or client.

formal.ex: Each [[timesheet]] must be submitted by the employee and approved by the line manager before the monthly payroll cut-off.
formal.ex_us: Each [[timesheet]] must be submitted by the employee and approved by the supervisor before the monthly payroll cutoff.

everyday.ex: Could you get your [[timesheet]] in by Friday, please?

note_fr: UK : « to fill in a timesheet » ; US : « to fill out a timesheet ». Évitez « time sheet of presence » ou « presence sheet » (calques de « feuille de présence »).

def: A short period during the working day when an employee stops working to rest.

formal.ex: Employees are entitled to an uninterrupted [[rest break]] of at least twenty minutes once they have worked six hours.

everyday.ex: Let's take a ten-minute [[break]] and pick this up again at eleven.

informal.ex: You've been at it since eight. Go and have a [[breather]].
informal.ex_us: You've been at it since eight. Go take a [[breather]].

note_fr: « To take a break » ou « to have a break » (UK), jamais « to make a break » ni « a pause ». En France comme au Royaume-Uni, vingt minutes de pause sont dues au-delà de six heures de travail ; le droit fédéral américain n'impose aucune pause.

def: The period in the middle of the working day when employees stop work to eat.

formal.ex: The [[meal break]] is unpaid and does not count as working time.
formal.ex_us: The [[meal period]] is unpaid and does not count as hours worked.

everyday.ex: I usually take my [[lunch break]] around one.

note_fr: « I'm at lunch » ou « I'm on my lunch break », pas « I'm in lunch pause ». Aux États-Unis, « meal period » est le terme des textes sur la durée du travail (wage and hour) ; certains États l'imposent, pas le droit fédéral.

def: A way of organising work in which different groups of employees work at different times of the day or night.

formal.ex: Employees engaged in [[shift work]] are covered by the specific provisions of the company agreement.

everyday.ex: Most of the production staff work [[shifts]].

note_fr: « To work shifts » ou « to work in shifts » = travailler en équipes. Ne traduisez pas « travail en équipes » par « teamwork », qui désigne le travail collaboratif. « Posted work » renverrait au détachement.

def: One of the fixed periods into which the working day is divided, or the group of people who work during it.

formal.ex: Each [[shift]] shall be followed by a rest period of at least eleven consecutive hours.

everyday.ex: I'm on the early [[shift]] all next week.

note_fr: UK : « early shift / late shift » ; US : « day shift / swing shift / night shift » (« graveyard shift » en familier pour la nuit). « Shift » désigne à la fois la tranche horaire et l'équipe : « the night shift has just arrived ».

fr: échanger son poste avec un collègue
def: To agree with a colleague that each of you will work the other's shift.

formal.ex: Employees wishing [[to exchange shifts]] must obtain the prior approval of their supervisor.

everyday.ex: Would you mind if I [[swapped shifts]] with Karim on Friday?
everyday.ex_us: Would it be okay if I [[traded shifts]] with Karim on Friday?

note_fr: « To swap » est le verbe britannique naturel ; les Américains disent plutôt « to trade » ou « to switch shifts ». « To pick up a shift » = prendre un poste supplémentaire. Évitez « to change my shift with », ambigu.

def: Working away from the employer's premises, usually from home, using digital tools.

formal.ex: [[Remote working]] is voluntary and requires the agreement of both the employee and the Company.
formal.ex_us: [[Remote work]] is voluntary and requires the agreement of both the employee and the Company.

everyday.ex: I'm [[working from home]] tomorrow, but I'll be on Teams all day.

informal.ex: [[WFH]] today - call my mobile if it's urgent.
informal.ex_us: [[WFH]] today - call my cell if it's urgent.

note_fr: « Teleworking » et « telework » existent (textes européens, administration américaine) mais sonnent administratifs : au quotidien, « working from home » ou « remote working ». Ne dites pas « I'm in telework » ; dites « I'm working from home ».

def: An arrangement in which employees split their time between the office and another place, usually home.

formal.ex: Under the [[hybrid working arrangement]], employees attend the office at least two days per week.
formal.ex_us: Under the [[hybrid work arrangement]], employees work on-site at least two days per week.

everyday.ex: We moved to [[hybrid working]] two years ago and nobody wants to go back.
everyday.ex_us: We moved to [[hybrid work]] two years ago and nobody wants to go back.

collocations: to work on a hybrid basis
note_fr: « Hybrid » se prononce /ˈhaɪbrɪd/ (« haï »), pas « i-brid ». Une offre d'emploi « hybrid » annonce un poste partagé entre bureau et domicile ; « remote » ou « fully remote » un poste entièrement à distance.

def: The days on which a hybrid employee is expected to work at the employer's premises.

formal.ex: The [[days of on-site attendance]] are determined by each department head in the light of operational needs.
formal.ex_us: The [[days of on-site attendance]] are determined by each department head based on operational needs.

everyday.ex: Tuesdays and Thursdays are my [[office days]].
everyday.ex_us: Tuesdays and Thursdays are my [[in-office days]].

note_fr: « I'm in on Tuesday » suffit à l'oral pour dire qu'on sera au bureau. « Anchor day » : jour où toute l'équipe est présente. « Presential » n'existe pas : dites « in person » ou « on site ».

def: To arrange in advance, through the employer's procedure, to be away from work on particular dates.

formal.ex: Employees must [[submit a leave request]] at least four weeks before the first day of the intended absence.

everyday.ex: I'd like to [[book leave]] for the last week of August.
everyday.ex_us: I'd like to [[request time off]] for the last week of August.

informal.us: to put in for time off
informal.ex: Have you [[put in for leave]] over Christmas yet?
informal.ex_us: Have you [[put in for time off]] over Christmas yet?

note_fr: « Poser des congés » ne se dit pas « to pose holidays » ni « to put holidays ». UK : « to book leave / holiday » ; US : « to request time off / PTO ». On « take leave » une fois la demande acceptée.

def: A formal request by an employee to be absent from work on given dates.

formal.ex: A [[leave request]] is deemed to be accepted only once it has been approved in the HR system.

everyday.ex: Your [[holiday request]] is still sitting with your manager.
everyday.ex_us: Your [[time-off request]] is still sitting with your manager.

collocations: to put in a leave request
note_fr: « Request » se construit avec « for » : « a request for leave », mais le verbe est transitif direct : « to request leave » (jamais « to request for »). « Demand » serait une exigence, pas une demande.

def: To give formal agreement to an employee's request to be absent.

formal.ex: Line managers shall [[approve]] or decline each leave request within five working days.
formal.ex_us: Supervisors shall [[approve]] or deny each leave request within five business days.

everyday.ex: Has Priya [[signed off your leave]] yet?
everyday.ex_us: Has Priya [[approved your time off]] yet?

informal.ex: My boss [[OK'd]] the Friday, so I'm off from Thursday night.

note_fr: « Valider » se rend par « to approve », pas par « to validate », réservé aux données ou aux billets. Refuser : « to decline » (soutenu), « to turn down » (courant) ; aux États-Unis, « to deny a request » est neutre, alors qu'il sonne sec au Royaume-Uni.

def: A day fixed by law or custom on which most people do not work.

formal.ex: Where a [[public holiday]] falls on a normal working day, employees shall suffer no loss of pay.
formal.ex_us: Where a [[legal holiday]] falls on a regular workday, employees shall suffer no loss of pay.

everyday.ex: Monday's a [[bank holiday]], so the office is closed.
everyday.ex_us: Monday's a [[holiday]], so the office is closed.

collocations: to fall on a public holiday
to work on a public holiday
note_fr: UK : « bank holiday » au quotidien. US : « holiday » tout court désigne le jour férié, d'où le risque de confusion avec « holiday » = vacances en anglais britannique (US : « vacation »). Ni la loi britannique ni le droit fédéral américain n'obligent l'employeur privé à accorder les jours fériés ; en France, seul le 1er mai est obligatoirement chômé par la loi.

def: To be away from work for one day with the employer's agreement.

formal.us: to take a day of leave
formal.ex: Employees may [[take a day's leave]] at short notice with the consent of their line manager.
formal.ex_us: Employees may [[take a day of leave]] on short notice with the consent of their supervisor.

everyday.ex: I'm going to [[take a day off]] next week to move house.
everyday.ex_us: I'm going to [[take a day off]] next week to move.

note_fr: « A day off » est un jour non travaillé, quel qu'en soit le motif ; « a day's leave » relève du congé officiel. « A free day » ou « a rest day » ne conviennent pas dans ce sens courant. Notez le génitif : « two days' leave ».

def: To be away from work with permission for a period of time.

formal.ex: Ms Durand [[is on leave]] until 14 August; urgent matters should be referred to her deputy.
formal.ex_us: Ms. Durand [[is on leave]] until August 14; urgent matters should be referred to her deputy.

everyday.ex: Tom's [[on holiday]] this week, so I'm picking up his calls.
everyday.ex_us: Tom's [[on vacation]] this week, so I'm picking up his calls.

informal.ex: She's [[off]] till Monday.

collocations: to be out of the office
note_fr: « On leave », « on holiday », « on vacation » : toujours « on », sans article, jamais « in holidays ». « Leave » est indénombrable : pas de « leaves ». Britannique : « holiday » ; américain : « vacation ».

def: A morning or an afternoon of leave or of work.

formal.ex: Leave may be taken in units of no less than a [[half-day's leave]].
formal.ex_us: Leave may be taken in increments of no less than a [[half day of leave]].

everyday.ex: I'm taking a [[half day]] on Friday, so I'll be gone by one.

note_fr: « A half day », pas « a half of day » ni « a demi-day ». Avec un trait d'union devant un nom : « a half-day session ». « Half a day » s'emploie aussi : « it took half a day ».

def: Time off work for a mother before and after the birth of her child.

formal.ex: The employee shall notify the Company in writing of the date on which she intends to begin her [[maternity leave]].

everyday.ex: Chloe goes on [[maternity leave]] at the end of March.

informal.ex: We need someone to cover Chloe's [[mat leave]].

note_fr: « To go on maternity leave », jamais « to take her maternity ». Différence majeure : la France et le Royaume-Uni prévoient un congé rémunéré par la loi, alors que le droit fédéral américain ne garantit qu'un congé non rémunéré, sous conditions (FMLA).

def: Time off work for a father or the mother's partner around the birth of a child.

formal.ex: [[Paternity leave]] must be taken within the period prescribed by law following the birth of the child.

everyday.ex: He's on [[paternity leave]] for the next few weeks.

note_fr: En France, le congé de paternité et d'accueil de l'enfant est aussi ouvert au conjoint ou partenaire de la mère : « paternity leave » couvre les deux cas au Royaume-Uni. Aux États-Unis, il n'existe pas de congé de paternité fédéral rémunéré ; on y parle souvent de « parental leave » ou de « bonding leave ».

def: Not to be at work when you would normally be expected to be there.

formal.ex: An employee who [[is absent from work]] must inform his or her manager before the start of the working day.
formal.ex_us: An employee who [[is absent from work]] must inform his or her supervisor before the start of the workday.

everyday.ex: Julie's [[off]] today - can I help?
everyday.ex_us: Julie's [[out]] today - can I help?

note_fr: À l'oral, « she's absent » fait scolaire : on dit « she's off » (UK), « she's out » (US) ou « she's away ». Le nom est « absence » ; « absenteeism » désigne le phénomène d'absences répétées, pas une absence isolée.

def: To tell your employer, in the way the rules require, that you will not be at work.

formal.uk: to notify the Company of an absence
formal.us: to notify the Company of an absence
formal.ex: Employees must [[notify the Company of any absence]] by telephone no later than one hour after their normal start time.

everyday.uk: to let someone know you'll be off
everyday.us: to let someone know you'll be out
everyday.ex: Just [[let me know you'll be off]] before nine, so I can sort out cover.
everyday.ex_us: Just [[let me know you'll be out]] before nine, so I can arrange coverage.

informal.ex: Two people [[called in]] this morning, so we're a bit thin on the ground.
informal.ex_us: Two people [[called in]] this morning, so we're a little short-handed.

collocations: to give as much notice as possible
note_fr: Construction : « to notify someone of something » ou « to inform someone of something », jamais « to prevent » (empêcher) ni « to warn » (mettre en garde). « To call in sick » = prévenir qu'on est malade.

def: To do a colleague's work while he or she is away.

formal.ex: During the Director's absence, the Deputy HR Manager shall [[deputise for]] her.
formal.ex_us: During the Director's absence, the Deputy HR Manager shall [[act for]] her.

everyday.ex: Could you [[cover for]] me on Friday afternoon?

informal.ex: I'm [[filling in for]] Sam while he's away.

note_fr: « To replace someone » signifie le plus souvent remplacer définitivement : pour une absence temporaire, préférez « to cover for », « to stand in for » ou « to fill in for ». « To deputise » (US « deputize ») suppose un adjoint désigné et reste surtout britannique.

def: The passing of information and responsibility for work to the person who will take it over.

formal.ex: A written [[handover]] shall be prepared before any absence exceeding two weeks.
formal.ex_us: A written [[transition of responsibilities]] shall be prepared before any absence exceeding two weeks.

everyday.ex: Let's do a quick [[handover]] on Thursday before you go.
everyday.ex_us: Let's do a quick [[handoff]] on Thursday before you leave.

collocations: to bring someone up to speed
note_fr: Le nom s'écrit en un mot (« a handover »), le verbe en deux (« to hand over one's files to someone »). Aux États-Unis, « handoff » est plus courant. Évitez « passation », qui n'existe pas, et « transmission », réservé aux données ou à la mécanique.

def: An automatic email telling senders that you are away and when you will be back.

formal.ex: Employees are asked to activate an [[automatic reply]] indicating their return date and an alternative contact.

everyday.ex: I've put my [[out-of-office]] on, with your name as the contact.

informal.ex: I'm [[OOO]] from Wednesday, back on the 12th.

note_fr: Formule type : « I am out of the office until 12 August with limited access to email. » On dit « out of the office » (avec l'article) dans la phrase, mais « an out-of-office » pour le message. « Absence message » n'est pas idiomatique.

def: To start working again after a period of leave or absence.

formal.ex: The employee shall [[resume work]] on the first working day following the end of the leave period.
formal.ex_us: The employee shall [[resume work]] on the first business day following the end of the leave period.

everyday.ex: I'm [[back]] on the 3rd, so let's talk then.

note_fr: « I'm back on Monday » (présent à valeur de futur) est la forme naturelle. Ne dites pas « I come back from holidays the Monday ». « To resume » est un faux ami partiel : il signifie reprendre, jamais résumer (« to summarise »).

def: The amount of work that a person or a team has to do in a given period.

formal.ex: The Company shall ensure that the employee's [[workload]] remains reasonable and compatible with his or her rest periods.

everyday.ex: How's your [[workload]] looking for the next fortnight?
everyday.ex_us: How's your [[workload]] looking for the next two weeks?

note_fr: Un seul mot. On parle d'un « heavy workload », pas d'un « big » ou « important workload » (« important » ne signifie jamais « gros »). « Charge » seul est un faux ami : frais, accusation ou responsabilité. « Fortnight » (quinze jours) est britannique.

def: The hours during which an office is normally open and staff are at work.

formal.ex: Requests received outside [[normal business hours]] will be dealt with on the next working day.
formal.ex_us: Requests received outside [[regular business hours]] will be handled on the next business day.

everyday.ex: You can reach me any time during [[office hours]].
everyday.ex_us: You can reach me any time during [[business hours]].

note_fr: « Out of hours » (UK) et « after hours » (surtout US) = en dehors des heures de bureau. Aux États-Unis, « office hours » évoque d'abord les heures de permanence d'un professeur ou d'un médecin : préférez « business hours ».

def: To continue working after your normal finishing time.

formal.uk: to work beyond one's normal hours
formal.us: to work beyond one's normal hours
formal.ex: Employees should not be expected [[to work beyond their normal hours]] save in exceptional circumstances.
formal.ex_us: Employees should not be expected [[to work beyond their normal hours]] except in exceptional circumstances.

everyday.ex: I had to [[work late]] three nights last week.

informal.ex: We [[pulled a late one]] on Thursday to finish the audit.
informal.ex_us: We [[pulled a late night]] on Thursday to finish the audit.

note_fr: « To work late » = travailler tard ; « to be late for work » = arriver en retard : ne les confondez pas. « To work long hours » décrit une habitude. « To stay on » (rester après l'heure) est surtout britannique.

def: To work extra hours later in order to compensate for time you did not work.

formal.uk: to make up the hours not worked
formal.us: to make up the hours not worked
formal.ex: With the manager's consent, the employee may [[make up the hours not worked]] within the same week.
formal.ex_us: With the supervisor's consent, the employee may [[make up the hours not worked]] within the same week.

everyday.ex: I've got a dentist's appointment at four, but I'll [[make up the time]] tomorrow.
everyday.ex_us: I have a dentist appointment at four, but I'll [[make up the time]] tomorrow.

collocations: to make up for lost time
note_fr: « To make up the time » et non « to catch up the hours » : « to catch up » s'emploie pour un retard de travail (« I need to catch up on my emails »). Attention, « récupérer » au sens de prendre un repos compensateur se dit « to take time off in lieu ».

def: The periods of the year when schools are closed, which many parents want to take as leave.

formal.ex: Requests for leave during [[school holiday periods]] will be considered in the order in which they are received.
formal.ex_us: Requests for leave during [[school vacation periods]] will be considered in the order in which they are received.

everyday.ex: Everyone wants the [[school holidays]], so get your request in early.
everyday.ex_us: Everyone wants [[school vacation]] weeks, so get your request in early.

note_fr: UK : « half-term » désigne les petites vacances de milieu de trimestre, et « term-time working » un contrat limité aux périodes scolaires. US : « spring break », « summer vacation ». Pas de « scholar holidays » : « scholar » = érudit.

def: To stop work before your normal finishing time.

formal.uk: to leave work before the normal finishing time
formal.us: to leave work before the normal end of the workday
formal.ex: Any employee needing [[to leave work before the normal finishing time]] must first obtain permission.
formal.ex_us: Any employee needing [[to leave work before the normal end of the workday]] must first obtain permission.

everyday.ex: Is it all right if I [[leave early]] on Wednesday?
everyday.ex_us: Is it okay if I [[leave early]] on Wednesday?

informal.ex: It's quiet, so let's [[knock off early]].
informal.ex_us: It's quiet, so let's [[duck out early]].

note_fr: « To finish early » est très courant au Royaume-Uni ; les Américains disent plutôt « to get off early » ou « to leave early ». « To knock off » (finir sa journée) est familier et britannique. Évitez « to go earlier », incomplet.

def: The legal limits on the number of hours an employee may work in a day or a week.

formal.ex: The [[maximum working time]] of forty-eight hours in any one week may not be exceeded save in the circumstances provided for by law.
formal.ex_us: The [[maximum hours of work]] of forty-eight in any one week may not be exceeded except in the circumstances provided for by law.

everyday.ex: With that much overtime, we're getting very close to [[the working time limits]].
everyday.ex_us: With that much overtime, we're getting very close to [[the limits on hours]].

note_fr: France : dix heures par jour et quarante-huit heures par semaine en principe, avec une moyenne plafonnée sur douze semaines. Royaume-Uni : quarante-huit heures en moyenne, sauf renonciation individuelle (« opt-out »). États-Unis : aucun plafond fédéral pour les adultes, seulement l'obligation de payer les heures supplémentaires.

fr: décompte / suivi du temps de travail
def: The system by which an employer keeps a reliable record of the hours or days its employees work.

formal.ex: The Company shall maintain a reliable system for the [[recording of working time]] and keep the records available for inspection.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall maintain a reliable system for the [[recording of hours worked]] and keep the records available for inspection.

everyday.ex: Our [[time recording]] is still done on paper, which is asking for trouble.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[timekeeping]] is still done on paper, which is asking for trouble.

collocations: to keep records of hours worked
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « timekeeping » désigne surtout la ponctualité (« his timekeeping is poor ») ; aux États-Unis, c'est le terme usuel pour le relevé des heures. En cas de litige sur les heures en France, l'employeur doit produire ses propres éléments de décompte : « the employer must be able to produce its records ».

def: The minimum uninterrupted period of rest an employee must have between two working days.

formal.ex: Every employee is entitled to a [[daily rest period]] of at least eleven consecutive hours.

everyday.ex: If she finishes at midnight and starts at seven, she isn't getting her [[daily rest]].
everyday.ex_us: If she finishes at midnight and starts at seven, she isn't getting enough [[time off between shifts]].

note_fr: Onze heures consécutives en France comme au Royaume-Uni (règle d'origine européenne). Il n'existe pas d'équivalent fédéral aux États-Unis : expliquez la règle plutôt que de chercher un terme. « Rest » est indénombrable ici : « eleven hours' rest ».

def: The minimum uninterrupted period of rest an employee must have each week.

formal.ex: The [[weekly rest period]] of twenty-four consecutive hours is added to the daily rest period and is, in principle, granted on Sunday.

everyday.uk: a full day off a week
everyday.us: a full day off a week
everyday.ex: Whatever the rota looks like, everyone has to get [[a full day off a week]].
everyday.ex_us: Whatever the schedule looks like, everyone has to get [[a full day off a week]].

collocations: to work six days in a row
note_fr: En France, vingt-quatre heures auxquelles s'ajoutent les onze heures de repos quotidien, en principe le dimanche. « Rest day » = jour de repos dans un planning d'équipes. Le droit fédéral américain ne prévoit rien ; quelques États imposent « one day of rest in seven ».

def: Work carried out during the night-time period defined by law or by a collective agreement.

formal.ex: Recourse to [[night work]] must remain exceptional and be justified by the need to ensure continuity of economic activity.

everyday.ex: He's been on [[nights]] for three years and wants to move back to days.

note_fr: « To work nights » ou « to be on nights » est bien plus naturel que « to do night work ». En France, le travail de nuit doit rester exceptionnel et être encadré par un accord collectif ; rien de comparable aux États-Unis.

def: A period during which an employee is not at work but must remain reachable and ready to act if needed.

formal.ex: Periods of [[on-call duty]] give rise to compensation, either financial or in the form of rest.

everyday.ex: I'm [[on call]] this weekend, so I can't go far.

note_fr: En droit français, l'astreinte elle-même n'est pas du temps de travail effectif, mais elle ouvre droit à une compensation ; seule l'intervention est du temps de travail. « Standby » est un synonyme fréquent. Avec trait d'union devant un nom (« an on-call week »), sans après le verbe (« she is on call »).

def: An occasion when an on-call employee is actually required to work.

formal.ex: Time spent on a [[call-out]], including travel to and from the site, constitutes working time and is paid as such.
formal.ex_us: Time spent on a [[callout]], including travel to and from the site, constitutes hours worked and is paid as such.

everyday.ex: I [[got called out]] twice on Saturday night.
everyday.ex_us: I [[got called in]] twice on Saturday night.

note_fr: « Intervention » est un faux ami : en anglais, le mot évoque une ingérence ou un acte médical. Dites « call-out » (UK), « callout » ou « call-in » (US). Point à expliquer aux clients : en France, le temps d'intervention, trajet compris, est du temps de travail effectif.

def: A system that lets employees choose when they start and finish work, within limits set by the employer.

formal.ex: The Company operates a system of [[flexible working hours]] under which employees may vary their start and finish times.
formal.ex_us: The Company operates a [[flexible work schedule]] under which employees may vary their start and end times.

everyday.ex: We're on [[flexitime]], so I tend to start at ten.
everyday.ex_us: We're on [[flextime]], so I tend to start at ten.

informal.ex: I've built up enough [[flexi]] to take Friday afternoon off.
informal.ex_us: I've built up enough [[flex time]] to take Friday afternoon off.

note_fr: UK : « flexitime » ; US : « flextime ». Ne confondez pas avec « flexible working » (UK), notion plus large qui englobe temps partiel, télétravail et horaires aménagés, et que tout salarié britannique peut demander.

def: The part of the day when all employees on flexible hours must be at work or available.

formal.ex: All employees must be present during [[core hours]], namely from 10.00 am to 12.00 noon and from 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm.
formal.ex_us: All employees must be present during [[core hours]], namely from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon and from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.

everyday.ex: Try to keep meetings within [[core hours]] so that everyone can make them.

collocations: to be available during core hours
note_fr: Plage fixe = « core hours » ou « core time » ; plage mobile = « flexible band » ou « flexible hours ». Notez l'écriture de l'heure : « 10.00 am » (UK, point) et « 10:00 a.m. » (US, deux-points).

def: An employee's right not to read or answer work messages outside working hours.

formal.ex: The employee's [[right to disconnect]] from digital tools outside working time is guaranteed by this agreement.

everyday.ex: People need to be able to [[switch off]] in the evening without feeling guilty.
everyday.ex_us: People need to be able to [[unplug]] in the evening without feeling guilty.

note_fr: Notion d'origine française, intégrée à la négociation obligatoire en entreprise. Il n'existe pas de droit général équivalent en droit fédéral américain, et le droit britannique ne le consacre pas dans la loi : présentez-le comme une règle française. « Disconnection right » est un calque.

explain.written: the right to disconnect, namely the employee's right under French law not to be contacted or to respond to work-related communications outside working hours, the practical arrangements for which are set by company agreement or policy
explain.spoken: In France employees have what's called a right to disconnect: outside working hours, they can't be expected to answer emails or calls.

def: The document setting out who may work remotely, how often, and on what conditions.

formal.ex: Eligibility for remote working is determined in accordance with the Company's [[remote working policy]].
formal.ex_us: Eligibility for remote work is determined in accordance with the Company's [[remote work policy]].

everyday.ex: Under the [[WFH policy]], it's two days a week at home, by agreement with your manager.

collocations: to be eligible for remote working
note_fr: En France, le télétravail est mis en place par accord collectif, par charte de l'employeur ou, à défaut, par simple accord entre l'employeur et le salarié. « Charter » passe mal en anglais des affaires : dites « policy ». « Agreement » s'il s'agit d'un accord négocié avec les syndicats.

def: Extra days off given in France to employees whose working week is longer than 35 hours, to bring their average back to 35.

formal.uk: days off in compensation for hours worked above thirty-five per week
formal.us: days off in compensation for hours worked above thirty-five per week
formal.ex: Employees working thirty-nine hours a week receive [[days off in compensation for hours worked above thirty-five per week]].

everyday.ex: On top of their five weeks' holiday, they get about ten [[RTT days]].
everyday.ex_us: On top of their five weeks of vacation, they get about ten [[RTT days]].

note_fr: Aucun équivalent britannique ou américain : gardez le sigle et expliquez-le une fois. Ne les présentez pas comme des congés payés (« holiday ») : ils compensent des heures effectuées. « Time off in lieu » est le parallèle le plus parlant pour un Britannique, « comp time » pour un Américain.

explain.written: additional rest days ('RTT days') granted to employees whose contractual working week exceeds the statutory thirty-five hours, so that their working time averages thirty-five hours over the year
explain.spoken: RTT days are extra days off. If your contract says 39 hours a week instead of 35, you get the difference back as days off.

def: To take a day's leave between a public holiday and a weekend so as to have four days off in a row.

formal.uk: to take leave on the working day falling between a public holiday and a weekend
formal.us: to take leave on the workday falling between a holiday and a weekend
formal.ex: The Company may require employees [[to take leave on the working day falling between a public holiday and a weekend]].
formal.ex_us: The Company may require employees [[to take leave on the workday falling between a holiday and a weekend]].

everyday.ex: Half the office is [[taking a long weekend]] around the 8 May bank holiday.
everyday.ex_us: Half the office is [[taking a long weekend]] around the May 8 holiday.

note_fr: « To make the bridge » ne veut rien dire. Les jours fériés britanniques et la plupart des jours fériés américains tombent un lundi : la pratique du pont est donc peu connue et demande une phrase d'explication. « Bridge day » est compris en Europe continentale, moins ailleurs.

def: To build up a right to paid leave gradually as you work.

formal.ex: Employees [[accrue leave]] at the rate of two and a half working days per month of actual work.

everyday.ex: You [[build up leave]] from your very first month.

collocations: to accrue on a pro rata basis
note_fr: « To accrue » est le verbe technique, transitif ou intransitif : « leave accrues monthly ». Évitez « to acquire holidays ». En France, deux jours et demi ouvrables par mois, soit cinq semaines par an ; aux États-Unis, l'acquisition dépend entièrement de la politique de l'employeur.

def: The amount of paid leave an employee has the right to take in a year.

formal.ex: The employee's [[leave entitlement]] for an incomplete year is calculated on a pro rata basis.

everyday.ex: What's the [[holiday allowance]] here - twenty-five days plus bank holidays?
everyday.ex_us: How much [[PTO]] do you get here - fifteen days plus holidays?

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « PTO » (paid time off) regroupe souvent vacances, jours personnels et parfois maladie dans un compteur unique, sans aucun minimum légal fédéral. Au Royaume-Uni, le minimum légal est de 5,6 semaines, jours fériés compris ou non selon le contrat. « Entitlement » = ce à quoi l'on a droit ; « allowance » = le quota accordé.

def: The number of days of leave an employee still has available to take.

formal.ex: The employee's [[outstanding leave balance]] appears on the monthly statement issued by the HR department.

everyday.ex: I've still got eight [[days left]] to take before May.
everyday.ex_us: I still have eight [[days left]] to take before May.

note_fr: « Balance » = solde (comme pour un compte bancaire) ; « remaining leave » ou « untaken leave » pour les jours restants. Ne dites pas « the rest of my holidays ». « Outstanding » signifie ici « restant dû », pas « remarquable ».

def: To transfer leave not taken in one leave year to the following year.

formal.ex: Employees may [[carry forward]] up to five days of untaken leave with the written consent of the HR Director.
formal.ex_us: Employees may [[carry forward]] up to five days of unused leave with the written consent of the HR Director.

everyday.ex: Can I [[carry over]] the three days I didn't manage to take?
everyday.ex_us: Can I [[roll over]] the three days I didn't manage to take?

note_fr: « To report » est un faux ami (rendre compte, signaler). Reporter des congés à l'année suivante : « to carry over / carry forward » (UK), « to roll over » (US). Reporter la date de ses congés : « to postpone » ou « to push back ».

def: The twelve-month period over which paid leave is earned and must normally be taken.

formal.ex: Unless a company agreement provides otherwise, the [[reference period]] for the accrual of paid leave runs from 1 June to 31 May.
formal.ex_us: Unless a company agreement provides otherwise, the [[reference period]] for the accrual of paid leave runs from June 1 to May 31.

everyday.ex: Our [[leave year]] runs from January to December.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[vacation year]] runs from January to December.

collocations: by the end of the leave year
note_fr: En France, la période d'acquisition court par défaut du 1er juin au 31 mai, ce qui surprend les interlocuteurs étrangers habitués à l'année civile (« calendar year »). « Reference period » est compris, mais « leave year » ou « holiday year » est le terme naturel au Royaume-Uni.

def: Time off given to an employee instead of payment for overtime worked.

formal.uk: time off in lieu of overtime pay
formal.ex: By agreement, overtime may be compensated by [[time off in lieu of overtime pay]].
formal.ex_us: By agreement, overtime may be compensated by [[compensatory time off]].

everyday.ex: I worked Saturday, so I'm taking Monday as [[time off in lieu]].
everyday.ex_us: I worked Saturday, so I'm taking Monday as [[comp time]].

informal.ex: I've got two days of [[TOIL]] to use up.
informal.ex_us: I've got a [[comp day]] to use up.

collocations: to take time off in lieu
note_fr: « In lieu » se prononce /ljuː/ ou /luː/ et signifie « à la place ». « TOIL » se dit /tɔɪl/. Attention : aux États-Unis, le « comp time » en remplacement du paiement des heures supplémentaires est en principe interdit dans le secteur privé pour les salariés « non-exempt ».

def: A period of leave that a parent may take to look after a young child, during which the contract is suspended.

formal.ex: An employee with at least one year's service may take [[parental leave]] or move to part-time work until the child's third birthday.
formal.ex_us: An employee with at least one year of service may take [[parental leave]] or move to part-time work until the child's third birthday.

everyday.ex: She's thinking of taking six months' [[parental leave]] after her maternity leave.
everyday.ex_us: She's thinking of taking six months of [[parental leave]] after her maternity leave.

note_fr: Le congé parental d'éducation français n'est pas rémunéré par l'employeur et peut être pris à temps partiel. Au Royaume-Uni, ne confondez pas « unpaid parental leave » et « shared parental leave » (partage du congé de maternité entre les parents). Aux États-Unis, « parental leave » désigne souvent tout congé lié à une naissance.

def: Time off work, agreed with the employer, during which the employee receives no pay.

formal.ex: Any [[unpaid leave of absence]] is granted at the Company's discretion and suspends the contract of employment.

everyday.ex: I've asked for a month's [[unpaid leave]] to go travelling.
everyday.ex_us: I've asked for a month of [[unpaid leave]] to travel.

note_fr: « Leave without pay » existe aussi (administration, US). « Leave without salary » est un calque. En France, le congé sans solde n'est pas prévu par la loi : il repose sur l'accord de l'employeur, ce qui le distingue du congé sabbatique.

def: A long period away from work, agreed with the employer, after which the employee returns to his or her job.

formal.ex: An employee who meets the statutory length-of-service conditions may apply for [[sabbatical leave]] of between six and eleven months.

everyday.ex: He's taking a [[sabbatical]] next year to sail round the Atlantic.
everyday.ex_us: He's taking a [[sabbatical]] next year to sail around the Atlantic.

informal.ex: After ten years in the job, I could do with a [[career break]].
informal.ex_us: After ten years in the job, I could use a [[career break]].

note_fr: En France, le congé sabbatique est un droit légal sous conditions d'ancienneté, que l'employeur peut seulement différer ou, dans les petites entreprises, refuser. Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, il relève du bon vouloir de l'employeur. On dit « on sabbatical », sans article.

def: Paid or unpaid time off given to an employee when a close relative dies or is seriously ill.

formal.ex: Employees are entitled to [[bereavement leave]] on the death of a close family member, as provided by law and the collective agreement.

everyday.ex: Her father died on Sunday, so she's on [[compassionate leave]] this week.
everyday.ex_us: Her father died on Sunday, so she's on [[bereavement leave]] this week.

note_fr: « Compassionate leave » (UK) est plus large que le deuil : il couvre aussi la maladie grave d'un proche. Les « congés pour événements familiaux » français (mariage, naissance, décès) n'ont pas d'équivalent unique : dites « statutory leave for family events ». Aux États-Unis, rien n'est imposé au niveau fédéral.

def: Absence from work without permission or without an acceptable reason.

formal.ex: Any [[unauthorised absence]] may result in a deduction from pay and in disciplinary action.
formal.ex_us: Any [[unexcused absence]] may result in a deduction from pay and in disciplinary action.

everyday.ex: He simply didn't [[turn up]] on Monday, and nobody's heard from him since.
everyday.ex_us: He simply didn't [[show up]] on Monday, and nobody's heard from him since.

informal.ex: He [[went AWOL]] for three days last month.
informal.ex_us: He was [[a no-show]] three days in a row last month.

note_fr: « Unjustified absence » est un calque : on dit « unauthorised absence » (UK, « unauthorized » aux US) ou « unexcused absence » (US). « AWOL » (/ˈeɪwɒl/, absent without leave) vient du vocabulaire militaire. Abandon de poste : « job abandonment » (US), sans terme britannique consacré.

def: The arrangements made so that an absent employee's work is done by someone else.

formal.ex: Managers are responsible for putting [[cover arrangements]] in place before approving any period of leave.
formal.ex_us: Managers are responsible for putting [[coverage arrangements]] in place before approving any period of leave.

everyday.ex: Who's providing [[cover]] while Amélie's away?
everyday.ex_us: Who's providing [[coverage]] while Amélie's away?

note_fr: UK : « cover » (indénombrable : « to arrange cover ») ; US : « coverage ». « Maternity cover » désigne à la fois le remplacement et le poste proposé à ce titre. « Replacement » désigne plutôt la personne qui succède définitivement.

def: The fact of arriving at work after the time you are supposed to start.

formal.ex: Persistent [[lateness]] will be dealt with under the Company's disciplinary procedure.
formal.ex_us: Repeated [[tardiness]] will be addressed under the Company's disciplinary policy.

everyday.ex: We need to have a word with him about [[being late]] every Monday.
everyday.ex_us: We need to talk to him about [[being late]] every Monday.

note_fr: « A delay » est le retard d'un train ou d'un projet, pas celui d'une personne : dites « he was twenty minutes late », jamais « he had a delay of twenty minutes ». « Tardiness » est courant en américain et vieilli en britannique. « I'm running late » = je vais être en retard.

fr: passer à temps partiel / réduire son temps de travail
def: To change from full-time work to working fewer hours or days each week.

formal.us: to move to a part-time schedule
formal.ex: An employee wishing [[to move to part-time working]] must submit a written request stating the hours sought and the proposed start date.
formal.ex_us: An employee wishing [[to move to a part-time schedule]] must submit a written request stating the hours sought and the proposed start date.

everyday.ex: She'd like to [[go part-time]] when she comes back - four days a week.

informal.ex: I'm [[cutting back]] to three days from September.

collocations: to go down to four days
to work four days a week
note_fr: « Travailler à 80 % » ou « au quatre-cinquièmes » : dites « to work four days a week », ou « 0.8 FTE » dans un tableau d'effectifs ; « to work at 80% » n'est pas clair. Au Royaume-Uni, la demande passe par le droit légal de solliciter un aménagement (« flexible working request »).

def: A unit that expresses part-time hours as a fraction of a full-time post, used to count staff.

formal.ex: Headcount is expressed in [[full-time equivalent]] terms as at 31 December.
formal.ex_us: Headcount is expressed in [[full-time equivalent]] terms as of December 31.

everyday.ex: The team is twelve people but only ten [[FTE]].

note_fr: Le sigle « FTE » se dit lettre par lettre. Aux États-Unis, « an FTE » désigne aussi, par extension, un salarié permanent à temps plein (par opposition à un prestataire). « Pro rata » (UK) / « prorated » (US) pour les droits calculés au prorata.

fr: temps de trajet / de déplacement professionnel
def: Time an employee spends travelling for work, as distinct from the ordinary journey between home and the usual workplace.

formal.ex: [[Travelling time]] between home and the usual place of work does not constitute working time.
formal.ex_us: [[Travel time]] between home and the regular place of work does not constitute hours worked.

everyday.ex: My [[commute]] is an hour each way, which is why I'd like two days at home.

collocations: time spent travelling to a client
to be compensated for travel time
note_fr: « Commute » ne désigne que le trajet domicile-travail ; un déplacement professionnel est « a business trip » ou « travel ». En France, le trajet inhabituel qui dépasse le temps normal n'est pas du temps de travail effectif mais donne lieu à contrepartie. Orthographe : « travelling » (UK), « traveling » (US).

def: Work carried out on a Sunday, which is restricted or specially compensated in some countries.

formal.ex: [[Sunday working]] is permitted only in the cases provided for by law and with the employee's written consent where so required.
formal.ex_us: [[Sunday work]] is permitted only in the cases provided for by law and with the employee's written consent where so required.

everyday.ex: Most of the shop staff [[work Sundays]] on a rota.
everyday.ex_us: Most of the store staff [[work Sundays]] on a rotating schedule.

note_fr: En France, le repos hebdomadaire est en principe donné le dimanche, avec de nombreuses dérogations (commerces, zones touristiques, continuité de l'activité). « Sunday trading » désigne au Royaume-Uni l'ouverture dominicale des commerces. Aux États-Unis, la question ne se pose pratiquement pas en droit du travail fédéral.

def: The minimum period of warning an employer must give before changing an employee's working hours or leave dates.

formal.ex: Any change to the distribution of working hours is subject to a [[period of advance notice]] of at least seven days.

everyday.ex: We need to give people at least a week's [[notice]] if we change the rota.
everyday.ex_us: We need to give people at least a week's [[notice]] if we change the schedule.

informal.ex: Thanks for the [[heads-up]] about Friday's shift change.

note_fr: « Notice » couvre à la fois le préavis de rupture et le simple délai de prévenance : le contexte tranche. « At short notice » (UK) / « on short notice » (US) = au dernier moment. « Prevenance delay » n'existe pas. Notez l'apostrophe : « seven days' notice ».

def: A period when the employer closes its premises and all employees must take leave at the same time.

formal.ex: During the [[annual closure]] of the plant, all employees are required to take three weeks of their paid leave.

everyday.ex: We have a two-week [[shutdown]] in August, so nobody gets a choice.

collocations: to keep days back for the shutdown
note_fr: En France, la fermeture de l'établissement impose la prise des congés, après consultation des représentants du personnel. Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur peut aussi imposer des dates en respectant un préavis. « Closing » seul désigne la clôture d'une opération ou des comptes.

def: The days of the week on which work is normally done, usually Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.

formal.ex: Leave requests shall be answered within ten [[working days]] of receipt.
formal.ex_us: Leave requests shall be answered within ten [[business days]] of receipt.

everyday.ex: It usually takes three [[working days]] to get an answer from payroll.
everyday.ex_us: It usually takes three [[business days]] to get an answer from payroll.

note_fr: L'anglais ne distingue pas jours ouvrés (du lundi au vendredi) et jours ouvrables (du lundi au samedi) : « working days » sera compris comme cinq jours par semaine. Pour des congés décomptés en jours ouvrables, précisez « counted on a six-day week (Monday to Saturday) ». « Calendar days » = jours calendaires. « Open days » = journées portes ouvertes.

def: Frequent or habitual absence from work across a workforce, especially when it is seen as a problem.

formal.ex: The report analyses the causes of [[absenteeism]] at the Lyon site over the last three years.
formal.ex_us: The report analyzes the causes of [[absenteeism]] at the Lyon site over the last three years.

everyday.ex: [[Absence levels]] have crept up since the reorganisation.
everyday.ex_us: [[Absence levels]] have crept up since the reorganization.

note_fr: Orthographe : « absenteeism », avec deux « e ». Les professionnels RH britanniques parlent plus volontiers d'« absence » (« absence management », « absence rate ») ; « absenteeism » a une nuance de reproche. Taux d'absentéisme : « absence rate ».

def: Working hours that fall outside the normal working day, such as evenings, nights and weekends.

formal.ex: Staff required to work [[unsocial hours]] receive the enhancements set out in the collective agreement.
formal.ex_us: Staff required to work [[nonstandard hours]] receive the premiums set out in the collective bargaining agreement.

everyday.ex: Working in logistics means [[odd hours]], I'm afraid.

note_fr: « Unsocial hours » est une expression britannique consacrée (on entend aussi « antisocial hours ») ; aux États-Unis, « nonstandard hours » ou « off-hours ». « Shifted hours » et « atypical hours » ne sont pas idiomatiques.

fr: semaine de quatre jours / semaine comprimée
def: An arrangement in which an employee works full-time hours over fewer days than usual.

formal.ex: Under a [[compressed hours arrangement]], the employee works his or her full contractual hours over four days.
formal.ex_us: Under a [[compressed workweek arrangement]], the employee works his or her full contractual hours over four days.

everyday.ex: I do [[compressed hours]]: four long days, and Fridays off.
everyday.ex_us: I work a [[compressed workweek]]: four long days, and Fridays off.

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « compressed hours » (même durée sur quatre jours) et « a four-day week », qui peut désigner une réduction réelle du temps de travail. US : « a 4/10 schedule » ou « four tens » (quatre journées de dix heures). « Fortnight » est inconnu des Américains.

def: A system in which employees move regularly from one shift to another, for example from mornings to nights.

formal.ex: Production employees work a [[rotating shift pattern]] alternating between mornings, afternoons and nights.
formal.ex_us: Production employees work a [[rotating shift schedule]] alternating between mornings, afternoons and nights.

everyday.ex: We work [[rotating shifts]], so I'm on earlies one week and lates the next.
everyday.ex_us: We work [[rotating shifts]], so I'm on days one week and evenings the next.

note_fr: « On earlies / on lates / on nights » : pluriel familier typiquement britannique pour dire de quelle équipe on est. « Roulement » ne se traduit pas par « rolling » dans ce sens, sauf dans « a rolling rota » (planning tournant).

fr: congés perdus s'ils ne sont pas pris
def: A rule under which leave not taken by a given date can no longer be taken or paid.

formal.ex: Leave not taken by the end of the reference period shall [[be forfeited]], save where the employee was prevented from taking it.

everyday.ex: It's [[use it or lose it]] here, so do book your remaining days before May.

collocations: to be prevented from taking leave
note_fr: « To forfeit » = perdre un droit ; « leave lapses » = les congés sont perdus. Prudence sur le fond : en France comme au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur doit avoir mis le salarié en mesure de prendre ses congés, faute de quoi ils ne sont pas perdus. Certains États américains interdisent ces clauses.

fr: congé pour enfant malade / urgence familiale
def: Short, usually unpaid, time off to deal with an emergency involving a child or another person who depends on you.

formal.ex: An employee may take reasonable [[time off for dependants]] in order to deal with an unexpected emergency.
formal.ex_us: An employee may take [[family leave]] in order to care for a child with a serious health condition, subject to the eligibility conditions.

everyday.uk: time off to look after a sick child
everyday.us: time off to take care of a sick kid
everyday.ex: I need [[time off to look after a sick child]] - my daughter's got a temperature.
everyday.ex_us: I need [[time off to take care of a sick kid]] - my daughter's running a fever.

note_fr: Orthographe : le nom est « dependant » au Royaume-Uni, « dependent » aux États-Unis (où l'adjectif et le nom s'écrivent pareil). Le droit britannique accorde un temps « raisonnable », non rémunéré, pour les urgences ; le congé français pour enfant malade est lui aussi non rémunéré, sauf convention plus favorable.

def: The day on which an employee is due to come back to work after a period of leave.

formal.ex: The employee shall confirm her [[expected date of return]] in writing no later than eight weeks before the end of her leave.

everyday.ex: Do we have a firm [[return date]] for Nadia yet?

note_fr: « She's due back on the 5th » = elle doit reprendre le 5. Avancer une date : « to bring forward » (UK) / « to move up » (US) ; la repousser : « to push back ». « To advance a date » est ambigu.

def: Time during which the employee is at the employer's disposal and must follow its instructions, without being free to attend to personal matters.

formal.ex: Breaks during which the employee is free to attend to personal matters do not constitute [[actual working time]].
formal.ex_us: Breaks during which the employee is free to attend to personal matters do not constitute [[hours worked]].

everyday.uk: time that counts as working time
everyday.us: time that counts as hours worked
everyday.ex: The real question is whether changing into uniform is [[time that counts as working time]].
everyday.ex_us: The real question is whether changing into uniform is [[time that counts as hours worked]].

collocations: to be at the employer's disposal
to be treated as working time
note_fr: « Effective working time » est un demi-calque : « effective » signifie efficace. Préférez « actual working time », ou « working time » tout court (terme de la directive européenne). Aux États-Unis, la notion voisine est « hours worked » ou « compensable time ». Certaines absences sont « assimilées » à du temps de travail effectif : « treated as working time ».

def: The number of overtime hours per employee per year beyond which French law requires additional compensatory rest.

formal.ex: Overtime worked in excess of the [[annual overtime quota]] gives rise to compulsory compensatory rest in addition to the overtime premium.

everyday.ex: Several of the technicians will have used up their [[overtime quota]] by October.

collocations: a quota set by collective agreement
note_fr: Le contingent est fixé par accord collectif ou, à défaut, par décret. Ce n'est pas un plafond absolu : au-delà, les heures restent possibles mais ouvrent droit à une contrepartie obligatoire en repos et supposent la consultation du CSE. Aucun mécanisme comparable au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis.

explain.written: the annual overtime quota, being the number of overtime hours per employee per year, set by collective agreement or failing that by decree, beyond which additional compensatory rest is due
explain.spoken: There's a yearly allowance of overtime per employee. You can go over it, but then you owe people extra rest on top of the overtime pay.

def: Hours worked by a part-time employee above the hours in the contract but below full-time hours.

formal.ex: A part-time employee may be asked to work [[additional hours]] only within the limits laid down by law and by the contract.

everyday.ex: She's contracted for twenty-four hours, but she's been doing a lot of [[extra hours]] lately.

note_fr: Ne les appelez pas « overtime » : en droit français, les heures supplémentaires ne concernent que le dépassement de la durée légale par un salarié à temps plein. Les heures complémentaires sont plafonnées et majorées. Au Royaume-Uni, les heures d'un salarié à temps partiel au-delà du contrat sont simplement des « additional hours », en général sans majoration.

explain.written: additional hours ('heures complémentaires'), namely hours worked by a part-time employee beyond his or her contractual hours, which are capped by law and attract a pay supplement
explain.spoken: For part-timers we don't talk about overtime. Hours above their contract are called additional hours, and there's a cap on them.

def: A French scheme allowing employees to save up untaken leave or rest days, and sometimes pay, to use later as paid time off or money.

formal.ex: Employees may credit up to five days of untaken leave per year to their [[time savings account]], as provided by the company agreement.

everyday.ex: A lot of the senior people [[bank days]] every year towards a long break before retirement.
everyday.ex_us: A lot of the senior people [[bank days]] every year toward a long break before retirement.

collocations: to pay days into the account
note_fr: Dispositif français mis en place par accord collectif, sans équivalent direct. Le parallèle le plus proche est le « leave bank » américain ou le « holiday banking » de certains employeurs britanniques. Gardez le sigle CET et expliquez-le. « Saving account of time » est un calque.

explain.written: a time savings account ('compte épargne-temps'), a scheme established by collective agreement under which employees may accumulate untaken leave and rest days, or certain sums, in order to fund paid time off at a later date or to receive deferred remuneration
explain.spoken: It's a kind of savings account, but for time. You pay in days you haven't taken, and later you can use them for a long break or cash them in.

fr: annualisation / aménagement du temps de travail sur l'année
def: A system in which working time is counted over the whole year, so that weekly hours can vary with the level of activity.

formal.ex: Under the [[annualised hours arrangement]], weekly working hours vary between busy and quiet periods, and overtime is assessed at the end of the reference period.
formal.ex_us: Under the [[annualized hours arrangement]], weekly working hours vary between busy and slow periods, and overtime is assessed at the end of the reference period.

everyday.ex: We're on [[annualised hours]], so we do longer weeks in the run-up to Christmas and shorter ones in the spring.
everyday.ex_us: We're on [[annualized hours]], so we work longer weeks in the run-up to Christmas and shorter ones in the spring.

collocations: to average hours over the year
to smooth pay over the year
note_fr: En France, cet aménagement suppose en principe un accord collectif ; les heures supplémentaires se décomptent alors à la fin de la période de référence. Aux États-Unis, l'idée heurte la règle fédérale du décompte semaine par semaine pour les salariés « non-exempt ». Lissage de la rémunération : « smoothed pay ».

fr: salarié non éligible aux heures supplémentaires (statut « exempt », US)
def: In the US, an employee who is not entitled to overtime pay because of the nature of the job and the way he or she is paid.

formal.ex: As an [[exempt employee]], the Executive is not eligible for overtime compensation.

everyday.ex: Is she [[exempt]], or do we need to track her hours?

informal.ex: He's [[salaried]], so he doesn't clock in.

note_fr: Notion américaine issue de la législation fédérale sur les salaires et la durée du travail : les « exempt » (cadres, professions intellectuelles ou administratives remplissant des critères de fonctions et de rémunération) n'ont pas droit aux heures supplémentaires. C'est le repère le plus utile pour expliquer le forfait jours à un Américain, avec une réserve : le forfait jours exige un accord collectif et le respect des temps de repos.

fr: renonciation individuelle au plafond de 48 heures (UK)
def: In the UK, a written agreement by which a worker accepts working more than an average of 48 hours a week.

formal.ex: The worker may terminate the [[opt-out agreement]] at any time by giving the employer the agreed period of written notice.

everyday.ex: Most of the managers have [[opted out]] of the 48-hour week.

collocations: to opt out of the 48-hour limit
note_fr: Mécanisme britannique sans équivalent en France, où les durées maximales sont d'ordre public et où le salarié ne peut pas y renoncer individuellement. À signaler au client britannique qui voudrait faire signer un « opt-out » à ses salariés français : la clause serait sans effet.

def: Official permission not to apply a legal rule in particular circumstances.

formal.ex: A [[derogation]] from the daily rest period may be provided for by collective agreement, subject to equivalent compensatory rest.
formal.ex_us: An [[exemption]] from the daily rest period may be provided for by collective bargaining agreement, subject to equivalent compensatory rest.

everyday.ex: There's an [[exception]] for seasonal work, but it's a narrow one.

note_fr: « Derogation » appartient au vocabulaire du droit européen et reste compris des juristes britanniques ; un Américain dira « exemption », « exception » ou « waiver ». Faux ami : « derogatory » signifie péjoratif, dénigrant, et n'a rien à voir avec une dérogation.

fr: amplitude de la journée de travail
def: The total time between the moment an employee starts work and the moment he or she finishes, breaks included.

formal.ex: The [[span of the working day]], breaks included, may not exceed thirteen hours.
formal.ex_us: The [[span of the workday]], breaks included, may not exceed thirteen hours.

everyday.uk: the length of the day from start to finish
everyday.us: the length of the day from start to finish
everyday.ex: It's not the hours worked that worry me, it's [[the length of the day from start to finish]].

note_fr: Notion française déduite du repos quotidien de onze heures (vingt-quatre heures moins onze). « Amplitude » existe en anglais mais relève de la physique : dites « span » ou, à l'américaine, « spread of hours » (terme connu dans certains États).

explain.written: the span of the working day ('amplitude'), being the period between the start and the end of the employee's working day including breaks, which is limited as a consequence of the statutory daily rest period
explain.spoken: In France we also look at the whole day from when you start to when you finish, breaks included - not just the hours you actually work.

def: Additional paid rest that the law requires an employer to give, for example for overtime beyond the annual quota.

formal.ex: Hours worked beyond the annual quota give rise to [[compulsory compensatory rest]], which must be taken within the time limit laid down.
formal.ex_us: Hours worked beyond the annual quota give rise to [[mandatory compensatory rest]], which must be taken within the time limit laid down.

everyday.ex: Past that point they're owed [[extra rest]] as well as the overtime pay.

collocations: to take rest within a time limit
note_fr: À distinguer du « repos compensateur de remplacement » (« time off in lieu »), qui remplace le paiement des heures : la contrepartie obligatoire s'y ajoute. La directive européenne parle d'« equivalent compensatory rest » pour les dérogations aux temps de repos. Prononciation : accent sur « pen », /kəmˈpensətəri/.

fr: entretien annuel de suivi de la charge de travail (forfait jours)
def: The regular meeting at which the employer must discuss workload and work-life balance with an employee whose time is counted in days.

formal.ex: At least once a year, a [[workload review meeting]] is held to discuss the employee's workload, the organisation of his or her work and the balance between working and private life.
formal.ex_us: At least once a year, a [[workload review meeting]] is held to discuss the employee's workload, the organization of his or her work and the balance between working and private life.

everyday.ex: Have you had your [[workload check-in]] with Marc this year?

collocations: to keep a record of days worked
note_fr: Obligation propre au forfait jours : l'employeur doit suivre régulièrement la charge de travail et pouvoir le prouver, faute de quoi la convention de forfait peut être privée d'effet et le salarié réclamer des heures supplémentaires. Ne traduisez pas par « appraisal », qui désigne l'entretien d'évaluation.

explain.written: the periodic review meeting required for employees working under an annual working-days arrangement, at which workload, work organisation, work-life balance and remuneration are discussed
explain.spoken: For people whose time is counted in days, not hours, the employer has to sit down with them regularly and check that the workload is reasonable.

def: The employer's plan fixing which employees take their leave on which dates.

formal.ex: The [[order of leave]] is determined by the employer having regard to the employee's family circumstances and length of service.

everyday.ex: The summer [[holiday rota]] needs to be finalised by the end of March.
everyday.ex_us: The summer [[vacation schedule]] needs to be finalized by the end of March.

note_fr: En France, c'est l'employeur qui fixe l'ordre des départs, selon des critères légaux ou conventionnels (situation de famille, ancienneté), après avis du CSE, et il ne peut plus modifier les dates à l'approche du départ, sauf circonstances exceptionnelles. « To stagger leave » = échelonner les départs. « Departure order » ne convient pas.

def: Taking the main period of annual leave in several parts, which in France may give a right to extra days off.

formal.uk: splitting of the main period of leave
formal.us: splitting of the main period of leave
formal.ex: The [[splitting of the main period of leave]] may give rise to additional days of leave unless the employee has waived them in writing.

everyday.ex: If you [[split your leave]] and take part of it in the winter, you may get an extra day or two.

note_fr: Règle française : lorsqu'une partie du congé principal est prise en dehors de la période légale (du 1er mai au 31 octobre), le salarié peut avoir droit à des jours supplémentaires, sauf renonciation ou accord collectif contraire. Inconnue ailleurs : il faut l'expliquer en une phrase. « Fractioning » n'existe pas.

explain.written: the splitting of the main period of leave ('fractionnement'), which under French law may entitle the employee to additional days of leave where part of that leave is taken outside the statutory summer period
explain.spoken: If someone doesn't take all their main holiday in the summer period, French law may give them one or two extra days. It's a quirk, but payroll has to track it.

def: The practice of being at work for longer than necessary, or when unwell, in order to be seen to be there.

formal.ex: The survey points to a culture of [[presenteeism]] in which long hours are equated with commitment.

everyday.uk: staying late just to be seen
everyday.us: staying late just to be seen
everyday.ex: There's a lot of [[staying late just to be seen]] in that department.

informal.ex: Promotion there still depends far too much on [[face time]].

collocations: to be seen at one's desk
note_fr: En anglais, « presenteeism » désigne d'abord le fait de venir travailler malade, puis la culture des longues heures. « Face time » (en deux mots) = temps de présence visible au bureau ; ne confondez pas avec l'application. Le contraire recherché : « to manage by results, not by hours ».

def: Giving some of your own untaken leave to a colleague who needs time off for serious family reasons.

formal.ex: The [[donation of rest days]] is anonymous, unpaid and subject to the employer's agreement.
formal.ex_us: The [[donation of leave]] is anonymous, unpaid and subject to the employer's agreement.

everyday.uk: to give some of your leave to a colleague
everyday.us: to donate PTO to a co-worker
everyday.ex: Several people offered to [[give some of their leave to a colleague]] whose son was in hospital.
everyday.ex_us: Several people offered to [[donate PTO to a co-worker]] whose son was in the hospital.

note_fr: Le droit français permet à un salarié de renoncer anonymement à des jours de repos au profit d'un collègue, notamment parent d'un enfant gravement malade ou proche aidant. Aux États-Unis, des « leave donation » ou « leave-sharing programs » existent chez certains employeurs, sans cadre légal général. UK : « in hospital » ; US : « in the hospital ».

def: Leave taken to look after a relative who is seriously ill, disabled or losing independence.

formal.ex: An employee may take [[carer's leave]] in order to provide care for a dependant with a long-term care need.
formal.ex_us: An employee may take [[caregiver leave]] in order to care for a family member with a serious health condition.

everyday.uk: time off to care for a relative
everyday.us: time off to care for a relative
everyday.ex: He's asked for [[time off to care for a relative]] - his mother can't manage on her own any more.
everyday.ex_us: He's asked for [[time off to care for a relative]] - his mother can't manage on her own anymore.

note_fr: UK : « carer » ; US : « caregiver ». Le congé de proche aidant français, le « carer's leave » britannique et le congé familial américain (FMLA) reposent sur des conditions et des durées très différentes : n'employez pas l'un pour l'autre sans préciser le pays. « Helper » ne convient pas.

def: In the US, unpaid, job-protected leave that eligible employees of larger employers may take for certain family and medical reasons.

formal.uk: leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act
formal.us: leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act
formal.ex: Eligible employees may take up to twelve weeks of unpaid, job-protected [[leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act]] in a twelve-month period.

everyday.ex: She's out on [[FMLA leave]] until the baby is three months old.

informal.ex: He's on [[FMLA]] right now, so don't contact him about work.

note_fr: Loi fédérale américaine : le congé n'est pas rémunéré, ne vise que les salariés remplissant des conditions d'ancienneté et d'effectif, et couvre à la fois la naissance, l'adoption et la maladie grave du salarié ou d'un proche. Un interlocuteur américain raisonne à partir de ce cadre : le congé de maternité français rémunéré le surprendra. Certains États ont leur propre congé rémunéré.

def: A working day divided into two or more separate periods with a long unpaid gap between them.

formal.ex: The contract of a part-time employee may not provide for a [[split shift]] involving more than one interruption per day, save where a collective agreement so permits.
formal.ex_us: The contract of a part-time employee may not provide for a [[split shift]] involving more than one interruption per day, except where a collective bargaining agreement so permits.

everyday.ex: The cleaners work a [[split shift]]: six to nine in the morning, then five to eight in the evening.

collocations: a gap between two periods of work
note_fr: « Coupure » ne se traduit pas par « cut » : on parle de « the gap » ou « the break between the two parts of the shift ». En France, les coupures des salariés à temps partiel sont encadrées par la loi et les accords de branche.

def: An employee who regularly works a minimum number of hours at night and so benefits from special legal protection.

formal.ex: Any employee classed as a [[night worker]] is entitled to compensatory rest and to enhanced medical supervision.

everyday.ex: As [[someone on permanent nights]], he gets extra rest days.
everyday.ex_us: As [[someone on permanent nights]], he gets additional rest days.

collocations: to be classed as a night worker
note_fr: Travailler de nuit occasionnellement ne suffit pas à faire d'un salarié un « travailleur de nuit » au sens légal : il faut atteindre des seuils d'heures de nuit. La catégorie existe aussi en droit britannique (« night worker »), avec ses propres seuils ; elle est inconnue du droit fédéral américain.

def: A way of organising work in which three teams follow one another so that activity never stops over twenty-four hours.

formal.ex: The plant operates on the basis of [[continuous shift working]], with three eight-hour shifts in every twenty-four hours.
formal.ex_us: The plant operates on the basis of [[continuous shift work]], with three eight-hour shifts in every twenty-four hours.

everyday.ex: The line runs [[round-the-clock shifts]], seven days a week.

note_fr: « Three by eight » ne sera pas compris : dites « three eight-hour shifts » ou « a three-shift system ». « Round the clock » (UK) / « around the clock » (US) = vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre. La relève entre deux équipes : « shift changeover » ou « shift handover ».

fr: accord d'entreprise sur le temps de travail
def: A collective agreement negotiated at company level that sets the rules on hours, overtime and rest.

formal.ex: The [[company-level agreement on working time]] signed on 12 March takes precedence over the industry-wide agreement on these matters.
formal.ex_us: The [[company-level agreement on working time]] signed on March 12 takes precedence over the industry-wide agreement on these matters.

everyday.ex: Everything depends on what the [[working time agreement]] says about overtime.

collocations: to be covered by an agreement
in the absence of an agreement
note_fr: En matière de durée du travail, l'accord d'entreprise prime en principe sur l'accord de branche en France : point à expliquer, car un Américain associe « collective bargaining agreement » aux seuls sites syndiqués. Au Royaume-Uni, un « workforce agreement » peut jouer un rôle voisin en l'absence de syndicat.

def: To receive money in exchange for leave or rest days that you give up.

formal.uk: to convert rest days into remuneration
formal.us: to convert rest days into compensation
formal.ex: Subject to the employer's agreement, the employee may elect [[to convert rest days into remuneration]].
formal.ex_us: Subject to the employer's agreement, the employee may elect [[to convert rest days into compensation]].

everyday.ex: Can I [[cash in]] the RTT days I haven't used?
everyday.ex_us: Can I [[cash out]] the RTT days I haven't used?

note_fr: « To monetise » existe mais s'emploie pour un actif ou une audience, pas pour des jours de repos. UK : « to cash in » ou « to sell (back) leave » ; US : « to cash out PTO ». Rappel utile : le minimum légal de congés payés ne peut pas être remplacé par de l'argent, en France comme au Royaume-Uni, sauf à la rupture du contrat.

def: In France, one extra day worked each year without additional pay, linked to the funding of care for elderly and disabled people.

formal.ex: The [[day of solidarity]] takes the form of an additional day's work for which no further remuneration is due.
formal.ex_us: The [[day of solidarity]] takes the form of an additional day of work for which no further compensation is due.

everyday.ex: Whit Monday used to be the [[solidarity day]], but each company can now set its own arrangement.

collocations: to be set by company agreement
note_fr: Notion purement française, que vos interlocuteurs ne connaîtront pas : glosez-la toujours. Ses modalités (jour férié travaillé, jour de RTT en moins, heures réparties sur l'année) sont fixées par accord ou, à défaut, par l'employeur. « Whit Monday » = lundi de Pentecôte (UK) ; les Américains ne connaissent pas ce jour férié.

explain.written: the day of solidarity ('journée de solidarité'), an additional day of work per year performed without extra pay, introduced to help fund support for elderly and disabled persons
explain.spoken: Once a year French employees work one extra day without extra pay - it helps fund care for the elderly. Each company decides how it's done.

term.uk: payment in lieu of untaken leave

def: Money paid to an employee who leaves for the leave he or she has earned but not taken.

formal.uk: payment in lieu of accrued but untaken leave
formal.us: payment for accrued but unused vacation
formal.ex: On termination, the employee shall receive a [[payment in lieu of accrued but untaken leave]].
formal.ex_us: On termination, the employee shall receive [[payment for accrued but unused vacation]].

everyday.uk: to be paid for untaken holiday
everyday.us: to get paid out for unused vacation
everyday.ex: You'll [[be paid for untaken holiday]] in your final salary.
everyday.ex_us: You'll [[get paid out for unused vacation]] in your final paycheck.

note_fr: En France et au Royaume-Uni, les congés acquis et non pris sont payés à la rupture du contrat. Aux États-Unis, tout dépend de l'État et de la politique de l'employeur : ne présumez jamais du versement. « In lieu of » = à la place de.

def: The possibility for the employer or the employee to end a remote working arrangement and go back to working at the employer's premises.

formal.uk: termination of the remote working arrangement
formal.us: termination of the remote work arrangement
formal.ex: Either party may request the [[termination of the remote working arrangement]] by giving one month's written notice.
formal.ex_us: Either party may request the [[termination of the remote work arrangement]] by giving one month's written notice.

everyday.uk: to go back to the office full-time
everyday.us: to go back to the office full-time
everyday.ex: If it isn't working out, either side can ask to [[go back to the office full-time]].

note_fr: « Reversibility » serait compris d'un juriste mais n'est pas idiomatique : préférez « either party may end the arrangement » ou « to revert to on-site working ». Dans les entreprises anglo-saxonnes, « return to office » (« RTO ») désigne la décision de l'employeur de faire revenir tout le monde sur site.
